grey: Unique and permanent. It is quoted in the technical document, in every test result, and in every status call until the project closes. Never renumber one.

The requirement or requirements from the BRD that this solution answers. One solution can answer several. One requirement can need several solutions. STD means this is a standard piece of any implementation that nobody asked for and every site needs.
The part of the site or the mechanism. It groups solutions that share a shape.
What is being solved, in one line. Written so a business reader recognises their own request.
The Adobe Analytics variable or event that will carry the value. (M) means the variable is set as merchandising. (n) means the event is numeric. (c) means the event is a currency event.
The report name the variable will carry. This is what the business will see in Workspace, so it is agreed here and not later.
The format and a real example. Enough that a developer and an analyst read the same meaning.
The variables that go out on every hit, and the two page load solutions that carry them.
Everything from a product click to an order or a failed payment.
Search, account, forms, navigation, showrooms and errors.
The parts of the implementation that are settings rather than rules: report suites, marketing channels, classifications, filters.
The structure of the products variable, defined once because eight solutions depend on it.
Every slot in the report suite, used and unused. Consult it before assigning anything new.
Every change made after version 1.0, dated, with the IDs it touched.
